name: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury
definition: Partial or complete injury of the anterior cruciate ligament, commonly from non-contact pivoting or traumatic mechanisms, producing knee instability.

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is often clinical in acute sports injury.
investigations.MRI: MRI confirms ACL and associated meniscal/cartilage injury when required.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs exclude fracture and assess alignment.

amber: Reconstruction versus nonoperative care depends on instability, activity demands, associated injuries and patient goals.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Janu-sandhi/Snayu injury phenotype may be documented; ligament disruption remains a modern structural diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Partial or complete injury of the anterior cruciate ligament, commonly from non-contact pivoting or traumatic mechanisms, producing knee instability.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
